reason: VALUE/TRANSFER lens: refuted. The ceiling is small, the gate cannot be evaluated, and the node set changes by construction. (1) THE POOL HOLDS ALMOST NO REAL DIVISIONS. In x138 the candidate is an ORPHAN node at t+1 with a successor at t+2, and DeepCenter scores that point before the symmetry gate (add_safe_divisions_postlink, experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb). Only 35/151 GT divisions survive x138's gate stack even on GT geometry (CONTEXT.md l.736-744). DeepCenter rejects only ~16% of real geometric divisions (B32: DC>=0.20 keeps 97/116; 6bba, which DC never saw, is 125/151 of them, so this is roughly the held-out rate). About 0.6 of those have an orphan daughter. That leaves ~3/151 (~2%) of GT divisions in the rescue pool, i.e. ~1.1 on public (anchor TP19/FP13/FN21, D~53), inside ~111 rejected pairs per clip (444 on 4 dummies). (2) THE IMAGE CUE IS WEAK FOR THIS THRESHOLD. Our own measurement (experiments/RESULTS.md l.111, n=14) gives relative half-max volume -0.04 at lag -1 and -0.20 at +1/+2. The daughter/parent(t-1) ratio is therefore ~0.83 on average, above the 0.8 cut, so requiring BOTH daughters < 0.8 keeps only ~25-35% of real divisions. The same volume features gave nothing in the node pruner (RESULTS.md l.95). Valley < 0.85 plus sister 7-14 um keeps ~55% of GT (gtsister.csv). Expected public TP is ~0.35. (3) METRIC CEILING (anchor J 0.358): +1 TP = +0.00189, +1 evaluable FP = -0.00066. A perfect filter (1.2 TP, 0 FP) caps at +0.0023. Realistically (~2.3 rescued forks/clip, 2.7-5% evaluable-FP rate, neighbour daughters often cross-component) that is ~0.35 TP and ~3 FP = -0.0013. Optimistic 1/1 gives +0.0012, pessimistic 0/6 gives -0.0037. The precision estimate is ~4-15%, against a break-even of 0.265 on public and 0.11-0.20 on private, so the sign is negative in both. (4) NODE-COUNT/CLOSED-LINE ARTEFACT. Safe divisions run BEFORE filter_short_track_components (MIN_TRACK_LEN 6, KEEP_DIVISION_COMPONENTS). A rescued fork glues a short orphan tracklet to a long component, so tracklets that were deleted come back. The 'nodes identical' gate fails by construction, and any lab gain can come from node/edge recovery (the closed mirror/lowdet line) instead of divisions. Rescued forks also take used_sources ahead of the insertion, which perturbs #35's insertion set. (5) LB PRIOR. The only LB evidence on admitting DC-rejected forks is sjlee's threshold 0.20 -> 0.15, which scored 0.946 vs 0.947. B29 'veto OFF' +0.0024 locally was a single division event. This idea is a gated DC relaxation, i.e. K3b in disguise with a weak filter. (6) LAB GATE HAS NO POWER. The exp60 lab has 99 GT divisions, so we expect ~0.65 rescued TP in total. 'div_J up on both halves AND both embryos' needs at least one net TP in each of 4 cells. The 44b6 clips are DeepCenter in-sample (split_manifest train = 71 44b6), so a pass would be one noisy event. Realistic P(lab gate) is ~0.03-0.05, not 0.2.
fix: Drop it as a fork adder. If the division budget gets any hours, spend them on J-invariant fork REMOVAL (forkmid/forkblob), where the pool is dense in evaluable FPs. For the lab, only log a free diagnostic: in the exp60 presafe dumps, count the GT divisions whose second daughter was DC-rejected (the real pool size, which I estimate at ~2% of GT divisions) and the rule's TPR/FPR on those candidates. Revisit only if that count is >= 8 across the lab AND the rule's evaluable precision is >= 0.30 with node-set equality enforced: restrict the rescue to orphans whose tracklet already has >= MIN_TRACK_LEN nodes, and run it after the short-track filter. Never combine it with K3b, and never spend an LB slot on it before the R8 cutoff.
realistic_gain: Public ~-0.001 (range -0.0037..+0.0012; ceiling +0.0023 with a perfect filter); private ~-0.0003 (range -0.001..+0.0005; break-even 0.11-0.20 vs estimated precision 0.04-0.15). P(lab gate passes for a real reason) < 0.05.
